q: How does a copper smelter split its emissions between cathode and the sulphuric acid it sells?
title: Copper smelter: cathode vs acid
short: Sulphuric acid is made from the sulphur dioxide in smelter gas, so it is a co-product. Most smelters allocate shared emissions by mass or economic value and say which, while the acid plant's own energy goes to acid. Buyers of cathode and acid should each get a figure with the method stated.
audience: Copper smelters such as the one at Dahej, and buyers of their cathode, rod and acid

ul: Concentrate drying, smelting and converting fuel and power.
Gas cleaning ahead of the acid plant.

p: The acid plant's blowers and pumps, less any steam it exports. Acid plants often make surplus heat, which some smelters credit.
No. Copper and sulphuric acid are outside CBAM's current goods list, so these are product footprint figures for buyers, not customs data.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so a copper product figure can be traced back to the documents behind it. Factors outside India are entered from the official source and labelled.
